text: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.
The priests could not enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

All the Israelites saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD upon the house, and they knelt with their faces to the ground on the pavement, worshiped, and gave thanks to the LORD: "He is good; his mercy endures forever."
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

The priests stood at their posts, and so did the Levites with the instruments for the LORD's music, which King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD—"for his mercy endures forever"—whenever David offered praise through them. Opposite them the priests sounded trumpets, while all Israel stood.

Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat portions.
At that time Solomon kept the festival for seven days, and all Israel with him—an immense assembly, from Lebo Hamath to the Brook of Egypt.
On the eighth day they held a closing assembly, for they had celebrated the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.
On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the goodness the LORD had shown to David, to Solomon, and to his people Israel.

versions.text: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people home to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the goodness the LORD had shown to David, to Solomon, and to his people Israel.
versions.explanation: "home to their tents" is redundant when read aloud; "away to their tents" renders שִׁלַּח more cleanly without doubling the idea of going home.

text: So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the royal palace. Everything he had set his heart on doing in the house of the LORD and in his own house he carried through successfully.
Then the LORD appeared to Solomon by night and said to him: "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
If I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or command the locust to devour the land, or send a plague among my people,
and if my people, who are called by my name, humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
And now I have chosen and consecrated this house, so that my name may be there forever; my eyes and my heart will be there for all time.

versions.text: I have chosen and consecrated this house, so that my name may be there forever; my eyes and my heart will be there for all time.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew opens with וְעַתָּה ("and now"), a discourse marker that links this declaration to the preceding promise; its omission loses the connective flow of the divine speech.

text: As for you, if you walk before me as your father David walked, doing all that I have commanded you, and if you keep my statutes and my judgments,
then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with your father David when I said, 'You shall never lack a man to rule over Israel.'
But if you turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and worship them,

then I will uproot you from my land, which I gave you, and I will cast this house, which I have consecrated for my name, out of my sight, and make it a byword and an object of scorn among all peoples.
And this house, now so exalted, will appall everyone who passes by, and they will ask, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this house?'

versions.text: And this house, so exalted, will make everyone who passes by appalled, and they will ask, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this house?'
versions.explanation: "will make everyone who passes by appalled" is clumsy for oral reading and inverts the Hebrew construction, where the passerby is the one who is appalled. A direct verb ("will appall") reads more smoothly and keeps the sense of the Hebrew יִשֹּׁם.

text: And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them. That is why he has brought all this disaster upon them.'"
